parsed.rationale: This is LBBB rather than anterior MI: the QRS is wide (about 130 ms), with deep broad S waves in V1–V3 and broad monophasic R waves in I, aVL, V5 and V6; the ST elevation in V1–V3 runs opposite to the QRS and stays in proportion to the deep S waves (ST/S ratio about 0.17–0.27, borderline at most), with no concordant ST elevation or concordant ST depression in V1–V3, so it does not meet Sgarbossa or STEMI criteria.
